types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose. Also called Company, Corporation, Institution, Agency. Examples: Google, BBC Verify, Common Space, Governments.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Organization' class directly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and covers all mentions.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.embedding_query_text: AITool: A software application or system that uses artificial intelligence to perform specific tasks. Also called AI software, AI system, Intelligent agent, Machine learning tool. Examples: Earth AI tool, AI image generator Nano Banana 2, Gemini chatbot app, external AI detection tools.

chosen_type.label: SoftwareApplication
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'AITool' is a type of software application, and 'SoftwareApplication' is the most appropriate general class for the mentions.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: HowToTool
candidates.comment: A HowToTool is a HowToItem that is used but not consumed when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result. Also called instrument, utensil, equipment. Examples: a screwdriver, a mixing bowl, a hammer, a computer. Distinct from HowToSupply, which is consumed during the process.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

candidates.label: WebAPI
candidates.comment: An application programming interface that is accessible over web or internet technologies. Also called web service, API, REST API. Examples: the Google Maps API, the Twitter API, a weather data API.

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

types.embedding_query_text: Risk: A situation involving exposure to danger. Also called Hazard, Peril, Threat, Vulnerability. Examples: misinformation risks, misinformation, potential to spread misinformation, risks the feature posed.

chosen_type.label: Risk
chosen_type.definition: A situation involving exposure to danger or potential negative outcomes.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate captures the general concept of 'Risk' as a situation involving danger; existing candidates are too specific (medical) or refer to events.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any rule set or interactive tool used to estimate the risk of developing a complication or condition. Also called risk assessment tool, prognosis predictor, clinical risk model. Examples: a calculator for stroke risk, a scoring system for surgical complications. Distinct from MedicalRiskFactor, which is a single factor increasing risk.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskCalculator
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a complex mathematical calculation, often requiring an online tool, used to assess prognosis. Also called prognosis calculator, risk assessment tool, clinical prediction model. Examples: a calculator for cardiovascular disease risk, a tool for predicting cancer recurrence. Distinct from MedicalRiskScore, which is a simpler sum of risk factors.

candidates.label: PreventionIndication
candidates.comment: A PreventionIndication is a MedicalIndication for preventing an underlying medical condition, symptom, or disease. Also called prophylactic indication, preventative use. Examples: a vaccine for measles prevention, a medication to prevent migraines, dietary changes to prevent heart disease, exercise to prevent diabetes.

types.embedding_query_text: Report: A factual account or statement. Also called Document, Account, Record, Study. Examples: BBC Verify report.

chosen_type.label: Report
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Report' class directly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and the mention 'BBC Verify report'.

candidates.label: Report
candidates.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: ClaimReview
candidates.comment: A creative work that provides a fact-checking review of a specific claim. Also called fact-check, debunking, truth verification. Examples: A Snopes article debunking a viral claim, a PolitiFact rating of a politician's statement. Distinct from Review, which is a general assessment of an item.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

types.embedding_query_text: GroupOfPeople: A collection of individuals. Also called Team, Committee, Collective, Assembly. Examples: experts, bad actors, journalists, people trying to do work on the frontlines of rapidly evolving crisis scenarios.

chosen_type.label: GroupOfPeople
chosen_type.definition: A collection of individual human beings.
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Organization' is too formal for mentions like 'experts' or 'bad actors'; a more general type for a collection of individuals is needed.

mentions: people trying to do work on the frontlines of rapidly evolving crisis scenarios

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

types.embedding_query_text: Misuse: The improper or incorrect use of something. Also called Abuse, Misapplication, Mismanagement, Exploitation. Examples: misuse, abuse it.

chosen_type.label: MisuseAction
chosen_type.definition: The act of using something improperly or incorrectly, deviating from its intended purpose or function.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Misuse' is a specific kind of 'UseAction' that implies improper use, which is not covered by existing schema.org actions.

candidates.label: UseAction
candidates.comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.

candidates.label: ConsumeAction
candidates.comment: The act of ingesting or utilizing information, resources, or food. Also called consumption, utilizing, ingesting, using. Examples: Reading a book, eating a meal, watching a movie, using electricity. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.

candidates.label: LoseAction
candidates.comment: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.

candidates.label: WearAction
candidates.comment: The act of dressing oneself in clothing or accessories. Also called put on, don, attire oneself. Examples: wearing a coat, putting on shoes, wearing a hat.

candidates.label: DislikeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative sentiment or disapproval towards an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express dislike, disapprove of, show aversion, downvote. Examples: Disliking a movie, expressing disapproval of a policy, downvoting a comment online. Distinct from LikeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or approval.

types.embedding_query_text: Duration: The length of time that something continues or exists. Also called Period, Span, Term, Interval. Examples: 48 hours.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Duration' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE definition and the mention '48 hours'.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

types.embedding_query_text: Product: An article or substance that is manufactured or refined for sale. Also called Item, Goods, Merchandise, Offering. Examples: Google Earth, search.

chosen_type.label: Product
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Product' class directly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and covers the mentions 'Google Earth' and 'search' (as a service product).

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: A named day of the week. Also called Weekday, Weekend day, Calendar day. Examples: Friday, Thursday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'DayOfWeek' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE definition and the mentions 'Friday' and 'Thursday'.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: Policy: A course or principle of action adopted or proposed by a government, party, business, or individual. Also called Guideline, Rule, Regulation, Protocol. Examples: policies, our policies, guidelines built into its AI model, these guidelines.

chosen_type.label: Policy
chosen_type.definition: A course or principle of action adopted or proposed by a government, party, business, or individual.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate captures the general concept of 'Policy' as a principle of action; existing candidates are too specific (medical, boarding).

candidates.label: Course
candidates.comment: A Course is a description of an educational program or curriculum designed to impart knowledge, competence, or ability to learners. Also called educational program, curriculum, study program, academic course. Examples: "Introduction to Python Programming," "Art History 101," "Advanced Calculus," "Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from CourseInstance, which is a specific offering of a course at a particular time and place.

candidates.label: MedicalGuidelineRecommendation
candidates.comment: A medical guideline that recommends a process as efficacious, supported by sound data. Also called recommended guideline, best practice recommendation, medical advice. Examples: "guideline recommending statins for high cholesterol", "recommendation for early cancer screening". Distinct from MedicalGuidelineContraindication, which warns against a harmful process.

candidates.label: MedicalGuidelineContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical guideline that specifically designates a process as harmful, supported by sound data. Also called contraindicated guideline, harmful practice warning, medical prohibition. Examples: "guideline against routine antibiotic use for viral infections", "contraindication for specific surgical techniques". Distinct from MedicalGuidelineRecommendation, which suggests an efficacious process.

candidates.label: MedicalGuideline
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a recommendation made by a standard society or consensus statement on how to diagnose and treat a particular condition. Also called clinical guideline, practice recommendation, medical protocol. Examples: "AHA/ACC Heart Failure Guideline", "NICE guidelines for diabetes management", "WHO recommendations for vaccination".

candidates.label: BoardingPolicyType
candidates.comment: An Enumeration representing different policies used by airlines for boarding passengers. Also called airline boarding rule, boarding group type, flight boarding policy. Examples: "Zone boarding", "Group boarding", "Priority boarding", "Family boarding".

types.embedding_query_text: InputMethod: A means by which a user provides data or commands to a system. Also called Input device, Data entry method, User interface. Examples: text prompts.

chosen_type.label: InputMethod
chosen_type.definition: A means or technique by which a user provides data or commands to a system.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a general 'InputMethod'; existing candidates are specific types of methods or actions.

candidates.label: PaymentMethod
candidates.comment: A PaymentMethod is an intangible entity representing a standardized procedure for transferring monetary amounts for a purchase. Also called payment option, mode of payment, transaction method. Examples: Cash, CreditCard, BankTransfer, PayPal. Distinct from PaymentMethodType, which is a generic classification.

candidates.label: DeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: An enumeration describing a standardized procedure for transferring a product or service to a customer's chosen destination. Also called Shipping method, fulfillment method, delivery option, shipping carrier. Examples: Mail, freight, direct download, in-store pickup, UPS, FedEx. Distinct from DeliveryChargeSpecification, which specifies the cost of a delivery method.

candidates.label: UserInteraction
candidates.comment: An outdated general type representing any interaction a user has with a web page or content. Also called user activity, user engagement, web interaction. Examples: a user clicking a link, submitting a form, scrolling a page.

candidates.label: SolveMathAction
candidates.comment: The action of taking a mathematical expression and directing users to a resource capable of solving or simplifying it. Also called math solving, equation solving, calculation action. Examples: entering '2+2' into a calculator app, inputting a complex equation into Wolfram Alpha, using a math solver website.

candidates.label: PronounceableText
candidates.comment: PronounceableText is a data type for text that can be pronounced, often including phonetic or linguistic information. Also called phonetic text, spoken text. Examples: "schema.org" (pronounced "schema dot org"), "résumé" (pronounced "rez-oo-may"), a word with its IPA transcription.

types.embedding_query_text: Scenario: A postulated sequence or development of events. Also called Situation, Eventuality, Possibility, Outlook. Examples: false scenarios.

chosen_type.label: Scenario
chosen_type.definition: A postulated sequence or development of events, often used for planning, analysis, or simulation.
chosen_type.justification: A 'Scenario' is a conceptual construct or a postulated sequence of events, not an actual 'Event' itself, and no candidate fits this abstract meaning.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: CancelAction
candidates.comment: The act of asserting that a future event or action will no longer occur. Also called call off, revoke, annul, abort. Examples: Cancelling a flight, cancelling a meeting, cancelling a subscription. Distinct from ConfirmAction, which is asserting an event will happen.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: Imagery: Visual representations or descriptions. Also called Pictures, Graphics, Visuals, Illustrations. Examples: real satellite, aerial or 3D imagery, openly-accessible satellite imagery, satellite imagery, base layer of real satellite, aerial or 3D imagery.

chosen_type.label: ImageObject
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'ImageObject' is the most appropriate general class for 'Imagery' as visual representations, covering all mentions.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: Map
candidates.comment: A creative work that visually represents an area, showing features like roads, cities, or terrain. Also called cartographic representation, geographical chart, atlas page. Examples: a road map, a topographic map, a subway map, a world atlas.

candidates.label: ImageGallery
candidates.comment: An ImageGallery is a collection page web page type specifically designed to display a collection of images. Also called photo gallery, picture album, visual collection page. Examples: a wedding photo gallery, a portfolio of landscape images, a product image carousel. Distinct from VideoGallery, which displays videos, and MediaGallery, which is a more general type.

candidates.label: Photograph
candidates.comment: A Photograph, as a CreativeWork, is an image captured using a camera. Also called photo, picture, image. Examples: a portrait photograph, a landscape photo, a news photograph. Distinct from Painting, which is created with paint.

candidates.label: VisualArtwork
candidates.comment: A creative work that is primarily visual in nature, such as a painting, sculpture, or photograph. Also called art piece, visual art, artwork. Examples: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa, a Rodin sculpture, an Ansel Adams photograph.

types.embedding_query_text: Platform: A system that supports the operation of other software or services. Also called System, Framework, Environment, Medium. Examples: other platforms.

chosen_type.label: RuntimePlatform
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'RuntimePlatform' best fits the definition of a 'system that supports the operation of other software or services' among the candidates.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

types.embedding_query_text: View: A particular way of looking at or considering something. Also called Perspective, Opinion, Outlook, Stance. Examples: reliable view of the world.

chosen_type.label: Perspective
chosen_type.definition: A particular way of looking at or considering something; a point of view or understanding.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'View' refers to a perspective or understanding, not an action of viewing, and no schema.org candidate captures this abstract meaning.

candidates.label: ViewAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming or perceiving static visual content. Also called look at, observe, gaze upon. Examples: viewing a photograph, looking at a painting, examining a diagram.

candidates.label: WatchAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming dynamic or moving visual content. Also called view, observe, see. Examples: watching a movie, watching a live sports broadcast, watching a video tutorial.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

candidates.label: ClaimReview
candidates.comment: A creative work that provides a fact-checking review of a specific claim. Also called fact-check, debunking, truth verification. Examples: A Snopes article debunking a viral claim, a PolitiFact rating of a politician's statement. Distinct from Review, which is a general assessment of an item.

types.embedding_query_text: Legitimacy: Conformity to the law or to rules. Also called Validity, Authenticity, Legality, Justification. Examples: Google's legitimacy.

chosen_type.label: Legitimacy
chosen_type.definition: The quality or state of being in conformity with law, rules, or accepted principles.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate captures the abstract quality of 'Legitimacy'; existing candidates are specific legal documents, levels, or statuses.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: LegalForceStatus
candidates.comment: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.

candidates.label: Permit
candidates.comment: A Permit is an intangible entity representing an official authorization issued by an organization. Also called license, authorization, pass. Examples: a building permit, a parking permit, a fishing license. Distinct from LegalService, which is a service, not the document itself.

candidates.label: ActionAccessSpecification
candidates.comment: An ActionAccessSpecification is an Intangible item detailing the requirements that must be met to perform a specific Action. Also called access requirements, action prerequisites, permission rules. Examples: "Requires login," "Subscription needed," "Age 18+," "Admin privileges."

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

types.embedding_query_text: ImageContent: The subject matter or elements depicted within an image. Also called Visual subject, Picture content, Depiction, Representation. Examples: collapsed Eiffel Tower, sinkhole swallowing the Great Pyramid of Giza, Russian tanks in Ukraine's capital, non-existent nuclear power plant in Iran.

chosen_type.label: ImageContent
chosen_type.definition: The subject matter, elements, or scene depicted within an image.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents the abstract concept of 'ImageContent' as the subject matter *within* an image, rather than the image file itself.

non-existent nuclear power plant in Iran

candidates.label: WebContent
candidates.comment: A general type representing any content accessible via the web, including web pages, websites, and their elements. Also called web content item, online content, digital web asset. Examples: a blog post, an entire website, an image embedded on a page.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: HealthTopicContent
candidates.comment: HealthTopicContent is web content about a specific aspect of a health topic, such as a medical condition, its symptoms, or treatments. Also called medical web content, health information article, wellness resource. Examples: an article explaining diabetes symptoms, a webpage detailing cancer treatments, a video on heart disease prevention.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: AdvertiserContentArticle
candidates.comment: An AdvertiserContentArticle is an Article that has been paid for or produced to the specifications of an external entity. Also called sponsored article, advertorial, native advertising, paid content. Examples: A blog post promoting a product written by an influencer, a sponsored news segment, an article funded by a brand. Distinct from NewsArticle, which is typically produced by independent journalists.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called Individual, Human, Being, Character. Examples: Henk van Ess, Henry Ajder, Bill Greer, Trump.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Person' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE definition and all mentions.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation or state. Also called Nation, State, Land, Realm. Examples: Iran.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Country' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE definition and the mention 'Iran'.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

types.embedding_query_text: Border: A line separating two countries, administrative divisions, or other areas. Also called Frontier, Boundary, Demarcation, Edge. Examples: US-Mexico border.

chosen_type.label: Border
chosen_type.definition: A line or boundary separating two geographical or administrative areas.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a geographical 'Border' as a boundary line; existing candidates are administrative areas or regions.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A particular place or position. Also called Place, Site, Spot, Area. Examples: Gaza, conflict zones, White House lawn, hard to reach areas.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Place' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE 'Location' and covers all mentions.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: CampingPitch
candidates.comment: An individual outdoor space for overnight stay, typically part of a larger camping site or campground. Also called tent pitch, RV pitch, caravan pitch, campsite spot. Examples: Tent site #3 at Yosemite, RV spot at KOA, a designated area for a caravan. Distinct from Campground, which is the larger site containing multiple pitches.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

types.embedding_query_text: Watermark: A faint design made in some paper during manufacture, which is visible when held against the light and typically identifies the maker or the quality of the paper. In digital context, an embedded identifier. Also called Mark, Imprint, Signature, Identifier. Examples: invisible watermarks.

chosen_type.label: Watermark
chosen_type.definition: A faint design or embedded identifier, typically used to mark or protect content.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a 'Watermark' as an embedded identifier or design; existing candidates are documents or brands.

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. Examples: a personal reminder in a digital format, a draft of an idea, a quick thought saved electronically. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is intended for public consumption.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: DigitalDocumentPermission
candidates.comment: An intangible entity defining the access rights granted to a specific person or group for a particular digital document. Also called File permission, access control, document rights, sharing setting. Examples: "Read-only access for John Doe", "Edit permission for the Marketing Team", "View and comment access for all users". Distinct from DigitalDocumentPermissionType, which is an enumeration of possible permission types.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

candidates.label: Brand
candidates.comment: A Brand is an Intangible entity representing a name, symbol, or design used by an organization to identify and distinguish its products or services. Also called product line, trademark, label, marque. Examples: Nike, Apple, Coca-Cola, Google.

types.embedding_query_text: Feature: A distinctive attribute or aspect of something. Also called Characteristic, Quality, Aspect, Component. Examples: Lens feature.

chosen_type.label: PropertyValue
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'PropertyValue' class, defined as a 'feature of a product or place', is the best fit for the OIE_TYPE 'Feature' and the mention 'Lens feature'.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: ContactPoint
candidates.comment: A specific point of contact for an organization or person, such as a customer service department. Also called contact information, communication channel, service point. Examples: A customer support phone number, an email address for sales, a physical address for returns, a social media handle. Distinct from ContactPointOption, which is an enumerated option related to a contact point.

types.embedding_query_text: Topic: A matter dealt with in a text, discourse, or conversation; a subject. Also called Subject, Theme, Matter, Issue. Examples: harmful topics.

chosen_type.label: Topic
chosen_type.definition: A matter dealt with in a text, discourse, or conversation; a subject of discussion or study.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate captures the general concept of a 'Topic' as a subject of discourse; existing candidates are too specific or unrelated.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: HealthAspectEnumeration
candidates.comment: HealthAspectEnumeration is an enumeration of various aspects of health content, used to describe specific facets of health topics online. Also called health content categories, medical information facets, wellness topic types. Examples: 'Symptoms', 'Treatments', 'Causes', 'Prevention'.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: HealthTopicContent
candidates.comment: HealthTopicContent is web content about a specific aspect of a health topic, such as a medical condition, its symptoms, or treatments. Also called medical web content, health information article, wellness resource. Examples: an article explaining diabetes symptoms, a webpage detailing cancer treatments, a video on heart disease prevention.

types.embedding_query_text: Building: A structure with a roof and walls, such as a house or factory. Also called Structure, Edifice, Construction, Dwelling. Examples: UK parliament.

chosen_type.label: LegislativeBuilding
chosen_type.justification: The mention 'UK parliament' is a specific type of building, which is best represented by the 'LegislativeBuilding' class.

candidates.label: GovernmentBuilding
candidates.comment: A GovernmentBuilding is a civic structure that houses government operations or services. Also called public building, state edifice, official premises. Examples: city hall, parliament building, courthouse, post office. Distinct from GovernmentOffice, which is a specific type of organization within a government building.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: LegislativeBuilding
candidates.comment: A LegislativeBuilding is a government building civic structure where legislative bodies meet and conduct their work. Also called capitol building, parliament house, assembly hall. Examples: the U.S. Capitol, a state capitol building, the Houses of Parliament. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

types.embedding_query_text: Trust: Firm belief in the reliability, truth, ability, or strength of someone or something. Also called Confidence, Faith, Reliance, Assurance. Examples: public trust.

chosen_type.label: Trust
chosen_type.definition: Firm belief in the reliability, truth, ability, or strength of someone or something.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate captures the abstract concept of 'Trust' as a belief or confidence; existing candidates are documents or statements.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

candidates.label: Credential
candidates.comment: A Credential is a certificate or document used to verify the identity, qualifications, or authority of a person or entity. Also called certificate, qualification, accreditation, license, identification. Examples: A driver's license, a university degree, a professional certification, a digital security certificate.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: WarrantyPromise
candidates.comment: A structured value representing the duration and scope of free services provided for a product's defects or malfunctions. Also called product warranty, guarantee, service promise. Examples: a 1-year manufacturer's warranty, a 90-day repair guarantee, a lifetime parts warranty.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

types.embedding_query_text: SourceOfData: A place, person, or thing from which information is obtained. Also called Data source, Information origin, Data provider, Reference. Examples: trustworthy source of data.

chosen_type.label: DataSource
chosen_type.definition: A place, person, organization, or thing from which information or data is obtained.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate is general enough to represent a 'SourceOfData' which can be a person, place, or thing; existing candidates are specific types of data collections.

candidates.label: DataFeedItem
candidates.comment: A DataFeedItem is an individual entry or record contained within a larger DataFeed. Also called feed entry, feed item, data record. Examples: A single news article in an RSS feed, one product listing in an inventory feed, a single weather observation in a data stream.

candidates.label: Dataset
candidates.comment: A Dataset is a structured collection of information or data, typically organized for analysis or use. Also called data collection, data compilation, data repository. Examples: A spreadsheet of sales figures, a database of customer information, a collection of scientific measurements. Distinct from DataCatalog, which is a collection of multiple datasets.

candidates.label: DataCatalog
candidates.comment: A DataCatalog is a collection or repository of datasets, often providing metadata and access information for each. Also called data repository, dataset collection, data portal. Examples: A government open data portal, a university research data catalog, a scientific data archive.

candidates.label: DataFeed
candidates.comment: A DataFeed is a continuous stream or single file of structured information, typically updated regularly, about one or more entities or topics. Also called RSS feed, Atom feed, data stream, information feed. Examples: A news RSS feed, a stock market data feed, a product inventory feed, a weather data API.

candidates.label: CompleteDataFeed
candidates.comment: A data feed whose standard representation includes all current items, allowing older entries to be safely discarded upon refresh. Also called full data feed, comprehensive feed, complete item feed. Examples: An Atom feed of "Top Twenty Records" where all current records are present, a product catalog feed that always contains all available products, a news feed that provides all current articles. Distinct from DataFeed, which is a general feed that might only contain updates or partial information.

types.embedding_query_text: Occupation: A job or profession. Also called Profession, Job, Vocation, Career. Examples: geospatial analyst, AI and misinformation expert, AI-detection researcher.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Occupation' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE definition and all mentions.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: Attorney
candidates.comment: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.

candidates.label: EmploymentAgency
candidates.comment: An EmploymentAgency is a LocalBusiness that helps individuals find jobs and employers find suitable candidates. Also called recruitment agency, staffing firm, job placement service. Examples: A temporary staffing agency, an executive search firm, a headhunting company.

types.embedding_query_text: Role: The function assumed or part played by a person or thing in a particular situation. Also called Function, Position, Capacity, Part. Examples: co-founder of the non-profit satellite service Common Space.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Role' class directly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and is general enough to cover the mention 'co-founder'.

mentions: co-founder of the non-profit satellite service Common Space

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: Seat
candidates.comment: A specific seating location, often reserved, within an event venue or transportation. Also called reserved spot, seating assignment, chair, place. Examples: seat 12A on an airplane, row F seat 5 at a concert, a specific table at a restaurant.

candidates.label: LinkRole
candidates.comment: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.

types.embedding_query_text: Access: The means or opportunity to approach or enter a place, or to use or obtain something. Also called Entry, Admission, Availability, Permission. Examples: access to data.

chosen_type.label: ServiceChannel
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'ServiceChannel' class, defined as a 'means or method for accessing a service', is the best fit for 'Access' to data.

candidates.label: EntryPoint
candidates.comment: An EntryPoint is an Intangible representing a specific access point within a Web-based protocol. Also called API endpoint, access point, URL entry. Examples: A specific URL for an API call, a login page, a download link, a search form action URL.

candidates.label: AuthorizeAction
candidates.comment: An AuthorizeAction is an AllocateAction representing the act of granting permission or approval for an object or action. Also called grant permission, approve, sanction, permit, allow. Examples: authorizing a payment, granting access to a file, approving a request, permitting a user to perform an action. Distinct from AuthenticateAction, which is about verifying identity, whereas AuthorizeAction is about granting permissions after identity is verified.

candidates.label: ServiceChannel
candidates.comment: A specific means or method for accessing a service, such as a website, phone number, or physical office. Also called access point, service delivery method, contact channel, customer touchpoint. Examples: a company's customer service hotline, an online booking portal, a government agency's physical office, a mobile app.

candidates.label: LoginAction
candidates.comment: The action of gaining access to a device or application by providing credentials. Also called sign in, log on, user authentication. Examples: logging into a website, signing into a mobile app, logging onto a computer. Distinct from ControlAction, which is a broader category for actions that control something.

candidates.label: Ticket
candidates.comment: An intangible item used to grant access or confirm a reservation for an event, travel, or service. Also called pass, voucher, entry permit. Examples: a concert ticket, an airline boarding pass, a bus ticket, a movie ticket.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large town. Also called Metropolis, Urban area, Municipality, Town. Examples: Ukraine's capital.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'City' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE definition and the mention 'Ukraine's capital'.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

types.embedding_query_text: Landmark: An object or feature of a landscape or town that is easily seen and recognized from a distance and can be used as a guide. Also called Monument, Icon, Site, Reference point. Examples: Great Pyramid of Giza, Eiffel Tower.

chosen_type.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE definition and all mentions.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Mountain
candidates.comment: A landform that is a large natural elevation of the earth's surface, typically rising to a summit. Also called peak, mount, range. Examples: "Mount Everest", "Mount Fuji", "Rocky Mountains", "Mount Kilimanjaro". Distinct from Landform, which is a broader category for natural geographical features.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A particular day, month, or year. Also called Day, Calendar date, Specific date. Examples: 31/07/2026, Date: 31/07/2026.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Date' data type is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE definition and the mention '31/07/2026'.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.
